heading.en: One table for every normal curve

hook.en: There are endless *normal* curves, one for every mean and s.d., but we need only one table of areas. The trick is to change X into Z, which always has mean 0 and s.d. 1.
hook.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಸರಾಸರಿ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ವಿಚಲನೆಗೆ ಒಂದು ಪ್ರಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆ ಇದೆ, ಆದರೆ ನಮಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ ಕೋಷ್ಟಕ ಸಾಕು. X ಅನ್ನು Z ಗೆ ಬದಲಿಸುವುದೇ ಉಪಾಯ; Z ನ ಸರಾಸರಿ 0, ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ವಿಚಲನೆ 1.

title.en: Convert X to the standard normal variate Z
Read areas from the normal table (0 to z)
Solve problems on proportions and on finding μ and σ

say.en: There are endless normal curves, one for every mean and s.d., but we need only one table of areas. The trick is to change X into Z, which always has mean 0 and s.d. 1. In this lesson: Convert X to the standard normal variate Z.
Read areas from the normal table 0 to z.
Solve problems on proportions and on finding micro and sigma.

body.en: If $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)$, then $Z = \dfrac{X - \mu}{\sigma} \sim N(0, 1)$, with p.d.f. $\phi(z) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-z^2/2}$. The *normal* table gives the area from 0 to $z$. By symmetry, area from $-z$ to 0 equals area from 0 to $z$, and each half of the curve has area 0.5.
body.kn: X ~ N(μ, σ²) ಆದರೆ Z = (X − μ)/σ ~ N(0, 1). ಕೋಷ್ಟಕ 0 ಯಿಂದ z ವರೆಗಿನ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಮಮಿತಿಯಿಂದ −z ಯಿಂದ 0 ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣವೂ ಅಷ್ಟೇ; ಪ್ರತಿ ಅರ್ಧದ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ 0.5.

narration.en: If X sim N(mu, sigma^2), then Z = dfracX - musigma sim N(0, 1), with p.d.f. phi(z) = dfrac1root2pi e^-z^2/2. The normal table gives the area from 0 to z. By symmetry, area from -z to 0 equals area from 0 to z, and each half of the curve has area 0.5.

By symmetry, area from -z to 0 equals area from 0 to z, and each half of the curve has area 0.5. Z equals (X - micro)/ sigma has mean 0, s.d. 1.

title.en: Finding an area step by step

narration.en: The teacher converts marks to Z, sketches the curve, shades the area and reads it from the table.

say.en: Marks are normal with mean 60 and s.d. 10. Find the proportion scoring above 75.
Convert to Z: 75 minus 60, divided by 10, is 1.5.
Sketch the curve and mark z equal to 1.5. We want the tail to its right.
The table gives 0.4332 from 0 to 1.5. The right half is 0.5, so the tail is 0.5 minus 0.4332.
So about 6.7 percent score above 75. Out of 1000 students that is about 67.

narration.en: Marks are normal with mean μ and s.d. σ. Drag the two orange handles. Each is turned into a standard normal variate z = (x − μ)/σ, and the shaded area P(a < X < b) comes from the normal table: add the areas when a and b are on opposite sides of μ, subtract when on the same side.

Each is turned into a standard normal variate z equals (x - micro)/ sigma, and the shaded area P(a is less than X is less than b) comes from the normal table: add the areas when a and b are on opposite sides of micro, subtract when on the same side.

body.en: $P(Z > z) = 0.5 - A(z)$ and $P(Z < z) = 0.5 + A(z)$ for $z > 0$, where $A(z)$ is the table area from 0 to $z$. Between two values on opposite sides of 0, add the *areas*; on the same side, subtract. To find $\mu$ and $\sigma$ from given percentages, read the $z$ values and solve $x = \mu + z\sigma$ for both points.
body.kn: z > 0 ಗೆ P(Z > z) = 0.5 − A(z), P(Z < z) = 0.5 + A(z). ಸೊನ್ನೆಯ ಎರಡು ಬದಿಯ ಬೆಲೆಗಳ ನಡುವೆ ವಿಸ್ತೀರ್ಣ ಕೂಡಿಸಿ; ಒಂದೇ ಬದಿಯಾದರೆ ಕಳೆಯಿರಿ. μ, σ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯಲು x = μ + zσ ಸಮೀಕರಣಗಳನ್ನು ಬಿಡಿಸಿ.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. X ~ N(60, 10²). Find P(50 < X < 70) and P(X < 45). (Areas: 0 to 1 is 0.3413; 0 to 1.5 is 0.4332.)

say.en: Let us work this out together. X ~ N(60, 10 to the power 2). Find P(50 is less than X is less than 70) and PX is less than 45. (Areas: 0 to 1 is 0.3413; 0 to 1.5 is 0.4332.).
z for 50 and 70: minus 1 and plus 1 opposite sides: P equals 0.3413 plus 0.3413 equals 0.6826.
z for 45: 45 minus 60/10 equals minus 1.5.
PX is less than 45 equals PZ is less than minus 1.5 equals 0.5 minus 0.4332 equals 0.0668.
So the answer is P(50 is less than X is less than 70) equals 0.6826; PX is less than 45 equals 0.0668.

problem.en: In a normal distribution 31% of the items are under 45 and 8% are over 64. Find μ and σ. (Table: area 0.19 at z = 0.50; area 0.42 at z = 1.40.)

steps.en: Below 45 is 31%, so area from 45 to the mean is 0.19: z = −0.50, giving 45 = μ − 0.5σ.
Above 64 is 8%, so area from the mean to 64 is 0.42: z = 1.40, giving 64 = μ + 1.4σ.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. In a normal distribution 31% of the items are under 45 and 8% are over 64. Find μ and σ. (Table: area 0.19 at z = 0.50; area 0.42 at z = 1.40.)

say.en: Let us work this out together. In a normal distribution 31 percent of the items are under 45 and 8 percent are over 64. Find micro and sigma. (Table: area 0.19 at z equals 0.50; area 0.42 at z equals 1.40.).
Below 45 is 31 percent, so area from 45 to the mean is 0.19: z equals minus 0.50, giving 45 equals micro minus 0.5 sigma.
Above 64 is 8 percent, so area from the mean to 64 is 0.42: z equals 1.40, giving 64 equals micro plus 1.4 sigma.
Subtract: 1.9 sigma equals 19, so sigma equals 10 and micro equals 45 plus 5 equals 50.
So the answer is micro equals 50, sigma equals 10.
